questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere were there were also other international students and a good exchange program where they at the same time also had a good public health program.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The U.S. is a bit complicated to be an international student in at the moment. The Univerisity i was at was also kind of bad at answering when we had questions and providing the necessary information.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not very easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an orientation weekend which was very nice to meet the others and get some more info. But out contact person/the person in charge of the exchange was not very assisting with anything, however when we asked other people we found the information necessary and they were very helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They had a housing shortage and i was therefore housed at a hotel (shared room) the entire semster.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were serveral dining halls with a mandatory meal plan since we lived at a hotel and didn't have the option to cook.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Don't know becuase i didn't actually live on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a very good hotel and the satff there was very nice. I also lived together with most of the other exchange students which was really great.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's a little complicated and is often explained as if we should know how to do it already - i think they forget that we haven't been in this system before and do things very differnetly where we come from.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registering for classes is opened a bit before you arrive. You can look up the classes and exaplantions for the classes as well and then sign up through the myBU account. You can see on the same account in a differnt tab if you got into the class of were waitlisted. If you are waitlisted you have to contact the professor for that class to see if you can get in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Don't really know. You could contact the exchange advisor but she didn't respond until at least 2-3 weeks alter when the deadline was passed or the classes where maybe full.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was very successful. I was waitlisted for one class but talked to the professor and showed up for the class the first day eventhough i didn't get in yet and he ended up putting me in the class.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If there's a class you really want to get into but is full, talk to the professor and explain that you are an exchnage student and only have the oporunity to take the class this semester and why you want to take this class/why it is relevant for you and they will most likely be able to move some things around and get you in. And also wait to look at classes until the registration opens as most of the classes posted on the website beforehand will not be available once the registration opens.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had some really good courses in public health. However, courses in sustainability were lacking some nuance.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 x 700 point classes (highest level on master) and one 400 point class (highst level on BA)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. More discussion, teachers more involvoed with students and care about the outcome.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Disaster Management in Humanitarian Crisis 
Genetic Technologies for Public Health
NGO management and leadership
Healthy Climate Solutions (dropped this course)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would reccomened these courses:
Genetic Technologies for Public Health
NGO management and leadership

They were very interesting and i learned a lot of new things that i wouldn't get at my home university- The teaching style in these courses were also very different from what i was used to in a good way. The professors in these courses were also very involoved and really cared about the courses.

questions.answer:
Food was more expensive than i though and the mandatory health insrunce in the US.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had a very nice gym!!!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A very nice Gym!! and PDP-classes which are like extracurricular athletic courses.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: PDP-classes

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Cape-cod (rent a car and go there) and New York on weekend trip (take the train or the bus). 
See the Isabella Stewart Gardener musem. 
Explore Boston: the freedom trail, beacon hills, north end etc. 
Go see sportsgames: The red Sox at Fenway (baseball)(you can get student tickets for $9 if you sign up for something called the student9), The bruins (hockey) at TD gardens or the BU team at the BU arena or The celtics at TD garden (basketball) it's expensvie but worth it!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are generally very open so just say hey when you you sit down next to someone in class and they will strike up a conversation

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openess of people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Go to the events at BU - especially in the beginning, you will meet people there and they can be very fun. 
2. Get the mealplan even if you don't live on capmus (the get the part time one) as you will miss out on some social gatherings/dinners if you don't have it - some of my friends who lived off campus felt a little excluded sometimes because they couldn't join us for dinner, where we mostly hung out together
3. Sign up for PDP classes - they don't take ETCS but are a lot of fun and you get to meet non-exchange students here

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don't need to pay housing, dining plan etc. fees before you get there. I paid in the spring (like around beginning of April). They will tell you how to pay once you get there as it's a bit complicated when you don't have an american bank.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The political situation - there was a lot of emails from the immigration office regarding the Trump administrations restrictions for international students

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
